title: HK man, 38, allegedly steals S$347 earbuds from Changi Airport in August, arrested when he transited again in October

 HK man, 38, allegedly steals S$347 earbuds from Changi Airport in August, arrested when he transited again in October
 Officers from the Airport Police Division were waiting and arrested him in a planned operation
 Joshua Lee 
 November 16, 2026, 06:39 PM
Image credits: Changi Airport, Canva
 A 38-year-old Hong Kong man has been arrested for his suspected involvement in a case of shop theft at the transit area of Changi Airport Terminal 1. 
 The Singapore Police Force (SPF) said in a Nov. 16 news release that they were alerted to the case on Aug. 2, 2026, at about 12:30pm. 
 Preliminary investigations revealed that a retail assistant was conducting a stock check when she discovered a box of earbuds missing from a display shelf. 
 After reviewing CCTV footage, she established that a man had taken the earbuds, valued at S$347.71, at about 10:20am earlier that day and left the outlet without paying. 
 Arrested upon return
 With the aid of the CCTV footage, the police established the man's identity, but he had already departed Singapore. 
 However, when he returned to transit through Changi Airport on Oct. 29, 2026, officers from the Airport Police Division were waiting and arrested him in a planned operation. 
 Will be charged in court
 The man will be charged in court on Nov. 17, 2026, with the offence of theft in dwelling under Section 380 of the Penal Code 1871. 
 If convicted, the offence carries an imprisonment term of up to seven years, a fine, or both. 
 The police stated they take a serious view of shop theft cases and will deal firmly with offenders in accordance with the law.
